justification: Two-part setback correctness fix. PART 1 (engine): the capacity engine's DCP control selection. PART 2 (data gate): scripts/validate_dcp_setbacks.py + tests/test_dcp_setback_validation.py — the missing DETERMINISTIC semantic validator that catches setback values mislabelled vs their source clause (the class of defect schema validation, the change-only review queue, and the consuming-engine routing tests all let through; the initial bulk load never passed the human review queue). Multi-signal (CONFLICT, FOREIGN, MAGNITUDE, PLACEHOLDER); run live over 1001 rows it found 10 high-severity defects across 7 LGAs (burwood/camden/canada_bay/cumberland/fairfield/penrith/the_hills). A @pytest.mark.database ratchet locks the high-severity count at <=10 so a future extraction cannot add a mislabelled setback. No LLM is used (project deterministic-only rule); Gemini stays advisory-to-human triage. PART 1 detail: the capacity engine's DCP control selection. A statewide read-only audit of dcp_setback_controls (28 LGAs, 1001 current rows) found 62 groups where more than one current row shares the same (control_type, dev_type) — 53 legitimately tiered (lot-size/storey/street bands, with conditions) and 9 unconditioned/suspect (e.g. Burwood front_setback 9m AND 15m, both mis-extracted from non-setback clauses P8/P39). _get_dcp_value matched on (control_type, dev_type) and kept the LAST row in iteration order, ignoring the condition field, so the chosen setback was arbitrary and order-dependent. This makes selection deterministic and conservative: max(value_min) for minimum-requirement controls (largest setback = smallest buildable envelope = fail-safe, never over-reports capacity) and min(value_max) for prefer_max caps (tightest allowance); single-row callers are byte-for-byte unchanged. It also surfaces a data-gap when it had to choose between conflicting setback values, so the figure reads as verify-against-DCP rather than a single certain control. Pure in-memory function; no DB query/schema/IO change. Tier-accurate matching (parsing lot size/width/storeys from condition) is a separate, larger follow-up.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls (1001 current rows, 28 LGAs) is the source; fetch_dcp_setbacks returns all current rows with no dedup and minimal zone filtering. Confirmed via read-only audit that multi-row (control_type, dev_type) groups are common (62) and that _get_dcp_value previously consumed only the last matching row.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed one DCP value per control; in reality controls are tiered or sometimes duplicated/garbled, so several rows match. The condition field that distinguishes tiers was being ignored entirely by the selector.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Extends the existing _get_dcp_value rather than adding a parallel path; adds two small pure helpers (_matching_controls, _dcp_value_conflict) reused by the selector and the gap-flagging. No new DB query or table introduced.

functions.name: _get_dcp_value
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string, a dev_type string, and an optional prefer_max flag for cap controls
functions.output: a single float chosen deterministically and conservatively across all matching rows (max value_min, or min value_max when prefer_max), or None when nothing matches
functions.if_none: returns None when no row matches the control_type for the exact dev_type or the dwelling_house fallback, exactly as before

functions.name: _matching_controls
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string and a dev_type string
functions.output: every row matching control_type for the exact dev_type, or the dwelling_house fallback rows when there is no exact match
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when no row matches, so the callers treat it as no-control-available

functions.name: _dcp_value_conflict
functions.input: a DCPControl list, a control_type string and a dev_type string
functions.output: the sorted distinct value_min values when more than one exists (the selector had to choose), otherwise None
functions.if_none: returns None when zero or one distinct value exists, so no spurious conflict gap is raised

functions.name: conflict_groups
functions.input: a list of dcp_setback_controls row dicts (lga, control_type, dev_type, value_min, condition, source_text)
functions.output: one high-severity finding per (lga, control_type, dev_type) group that has more than one distinct value_min and no condition on any row to disambiguate
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when every group is single-valued or carries a disambiguating condition (legitimate tiered controls)

functions.name: fabricated_value_rows
functions.input: a list of dcp_setback_controls row dicts including review_reason and condition
functions.output: rows that store a non-null value_min while marking it assumed/standard-pattern — the hard-invariant violation (a guessed number presented as fact)
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when no row stores a guessed value, the required production state after the insert scripts write NULL for unverified rows

functions.name: value_absent_from_source
functions.output: advisory list of rows whose numeric value's digits do not appear in their own source text (likely silent guesses)
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when every value appears in its source; skips non-numeric values and empty source

functions.name: assert_clean_row
functions.input: a single row dict plus config (value_field, marker_fields, marker_pattern)
functions.output: nothing on success; raises ValueError when the row would store a value while a marker field admits it is assumed/guessed
functions.if_none: a row with an empty/NULL value passes even if marked assumed — the honest 'rule exists, value unknown' state is allowed

functions.name: conflicting_values
functions.input: rows plus key_fields, value_field and an optional condition_field; key components may be arrays (coerced hashable)
functions.output: one entry per key group holding more than one distinct value with no condition to disambiguate
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when every key group is single-valued or carries a disambiguating condition

functions.name: audit_setback_controls
functions.input: a list of dcp_setback_controls row dicts as fetched from the live table
functions.output: a flat list of findings across all four signals (conflict, foreign-language, magnitude, placeholder), each tagged high or advisory severity
functions.if_none: returns an empty list when no signal fires, meaning the extracted setback data passes the semantic gate

values: N/A - no new DB/API values read; operates on the already-fetched DCPControl list passed into compute_constraint_arithmetic.
queries: N/A - no SQL added or changed; the audit that informed this was a separate read-only probe, not part of the runtime path.

break_it.scenario: A tiered control list is passed in a different row order across two runs (DB ORDER BY changes, or re-extraction reorders rows)
break_it.what_happens: previously the selected setback flipped between tiers (last-row-wins), so the same lot could report different buildable areas run to run
break_it.repro: _get_dcp_value([front 9, front 15]) vs _get_dcp_value([front 15, front 9]) — covered by test_selection_is_order_independent
break_it.how: selection now reduces over ALL matching rows with max()/min(), so it is order-independent; the test asserts both orderings return 15.0

break_it.scenario: Conflicting setback values exist but the engine silently presents one as a single certain figure (the original Burwood 15m bug)
break_it.what_happens: a user sees an authoritative-looking setback/footprint built on an arbitrarily-chosen (and possibly mis-extracted) value with no warning
break_it.repro: compute_constraint_arithmetic with front_setback rows 9m and 15m — covered by test_burwood_conflict_uses_conservative_and_flags_gap
break_it.how: _dcp_value_conflict drives a gap listing all differing values and the conservative one used; the engine still picks the largest (smallest buildable) so it never over-reports capacity while the conflict is flagged for verification

break_it.scenario: A cap control (max_site_coverage) has two values and the change wrongly applies the minimum-requirement (max) rule, loosening the cap
break_it.what_happens: the engine would allow MORE site coverage than the tightest cap, over-reporting buildable area
break_it.how: prefer_max branch reduces with min() over value_max, so the tightest cap wins; the test locks 50.0

break_it.scenario: An exact dev_type control is diluted by dwelling_house fallback rows of the same control_type
break_it.what_happens: a secondary_dwelling setback could be mixed with dwelling_house values and mis-resolved
break_it.repro: _get_dcp_value with a dwelling_house front 6m and a secondary_dwelling front 3m, dev_type='secondary_dwelling' — covered by test_exact_dev_type_preferred_over_dwelling_house (expects 3.0)
break_it.how: _matching_controls returns ONLY exact dev_type rows when any exist; the dwelling_house fallback is used solely when there is no exact match

break_it.scenario: The validator false-positives on a legitimate tiered or terse setback row (e.g. 'lots 200-300m2: 3m', or 'One storey - 3.5 metres')
break_it.what_happens: real council controls would be wrongly flagged as defects, drowning the signal and eroding trust in the gate
break_it.repro: foreign_language / conflict_groups over a tiered row with a condition and a terse storey-tiered row — covered by test_conflict_with_a_condition_is_not_flagged and test_terse_storey_tiered_setback_not_flagged
break_it.how: CONFLICT only fires when NO row in the group has a condition; FOREIGN requires strong foreign-control language AND the absence of setback language and deliberately excludes bare 'storey'; magnitude/placeholder are advisory-only, so the live run yielded 10 high-severity (real) vs 53 advisory

break_it.scenario: A future extraction re-introduces a mislabelled setback (the exact Burwood regression) and silently reaches production
break_it.what_happens: the original class of bug recurs and a user sees a confident wrong setback again
break_it.repro: pytest -m database test_live_high_severity_within_baseline with a new bad row present pushes the count above 10 and fails
break_it.how: the database ratchet test asserts the live high-severity count never exceeds the recorded baseline (now 7 after quarantining 3 bad rows); any new mislabelled setback raises the count and fails the gate, naming the offending lga/control_type/signal

break_it.scenario: An import script can't find a real value and fills in a guessed default (the POS=24 / solar=3h 'assumed standard NSW' pattern), presenting it as a council rule
break_it.what_happens: fabricated data reaches production looking authoritative — exactly what happened with 27 assumed POS/solar rows
break_it.repro: fabricated_value_rows over a row with value_min set AND condition/review_reason marked assumed — covered by test_assumed_value_with_a_number_is_flagged and the live test_live_has_no_fabricated_values
break_it.how: LOCK #1 — insert_private_open_space.py and insert_solar_access_hours.py now write value_min=NULL for any needs_review row (records the rule exists, value unknown -> 'check council', never a guess). LOCK #2 — fabricated_value_rows + the live database test fail the build if any current row stores a number it admits is assumed; verified live = 0 after the fix.

break_it.scenario: The same fabricated/conflicting bug exists in other extracted tables (LEP land-use, SEPP standards) and goes unchecked
break_it.what_happens: the fix would be setback-only and the bug class would persist elsewhere in the database
break_it.repro: run conflicting_values/fabricated_values (services/extracted_data_integrity.py) against lep_land_use_table, housing_sepp_standards and the non-setback dcp_setback_controls types
break_it.how: the checks are generalised into a domain-agnostic engine (extracted_data_integrity) configured per table; validate_dcp_setbacks now delegates to it. Swept live: lep_land_use_table (17353 rows) 0/0, housing_sepp_standards (45) 0/0, non-setback DCP controls (708) 1 conflict / 0 fabricated — so the structured tables are clean and only the PDF-prose DCP table carried the bug. assert_clean_row gives a write-time gate so future fabrication is blocked at entry, not just swept after.

break_it.scenario: A future edit adds a guessed value to an insert script's row list, or breaks the NULL-for-unverified logic, and it only gets caught by a periodic cron
break_it.what_happens: fabricated data could enter and serve to users for a full cron cycle before detection
break_it.repro: add a verified row with a value plus an 'Assumed standard NSW' note to POS_ROWS and run pytest — covered by tests/test_insert_scripts_integrity.py
break_it.how: the two insert scripts now CALL assert_clean_row before every INSERT (write-time block), and tests/test_insert_scripts_integrity.py runs the same gate offline over the scripts' own row data on EVERY commit (no DB needed), so a guessed value fails the build immediately rather than waiting for the live cron.

post_merge.db_reset: N/A - no database change; the bad Burwood/camden rows in dcp_setback_controls are a separate data-quality follow-up (the engine now fails safe and flags them, but the rows still need correcting).
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - services-layer logic only; no Trigger.dev/frontend change. The intelligence brief and capacity card consume the same compute_constraint_arithmetic output and gain the conflict gaps automatically.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run the brief for an LGA with conflicting setbacks (e.g. 14 Stanley St, Croydon Park — Burwood front 9/15): the Development Yield card's footprint is now computed from the conservative setback and a Data Gap flags the conflicting front-setback values for verification. Run a single-setback LGA and confirm no conflict gap appears and the value is unchanged.
